md_name: iPSC to neuron neurodegeneration phenotype workflow
md_description: Workflow for patient-derived induced pluripotent stem cells differentiated into neurons to model neurodegenerative disease phenotypes. The DAG includes cell expansion and differentiation, capture of morphological and synaptic phenotypes, and downstream computational integration of these outputs for disease characterization and therapeutic intervention evaluation.

patient_derived_ipscs.reasoning: This is an Entity node, so I included only intrinsic identity/origin fields for the patient-derived iPSC lines: provenance, disease association, and genetic-variant context. I excluded any expansion, passage, differentiation, capture, or analysis fields because those belong to downstream Process/Capture/Derivative nodes. I also avoided sample/experiment identifiers that could be repeated elsewhere in the DAG, and kept the schema focused on what the iPSC lines are rather than what happens to them.

md_schema.descr: String identifier for the patient donor of the iPSC line, recorded at lineage/provenance assignment for the starting cell line; example format: PAT_001 or de-identified donor code. Use only if donor identity is tracked in the dataset.

Primary neurodegenerative disease linked to the donor-derived iPSC line, recorded as the known clinical/genetic context of origin. Use this to classify the line by disease model; examples include Alzheimer's disease or Parkinson's disease.

Genetic variant present in the donor background used to derive the iPSC line, reported at the entity level as a stable provenance attribute; use HGVS-style notation when available, for example c.2573T>G or p.Val600Glu.
Official gene symbol for the disease-linked locus carried by the donor-derived iPSC line, recorded as the intrinsic genetic background of the starting cell line; example: APP, PSEN1, LRRK2, SNCA.

Clinical interpretation of the reported variant for the donor-derived iPSC line, recorded as part of provenance/identity rather than as a measurement; use the most curated classification available from the source record.

Original somatic tissue source used to generate the iPSC line, recorded at the entity level if known; examples include skin fibroblast, peripheral blood mononuclear cell, or urine-derived epithelial cell.
Reprogramming approach used to generate the iPSC line, recorded as a stable origin attribute of the entity; examples include Sendai virus, episomal plasmid, lentiviral, or mRNA-based reprogramming.

ipsc_expansion_and_passaging.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included only expansion/passaging protocol parameters and maintenance conditions that describe how the iPSC cultures were handled before differentiation. I did not repeat intrinsic donor or line identity fields from the upstream Entity node, and I did not include downstream output properties of the expanded cultures because those belong on the output Entity node. I also avoided capture/signal/derivative content and kept software/hardware details out because this is a wet-lab process rather than an instrumented capture or computational step.

md_schema.descr: Basal medium used to maintain and expand the iPSC cultures during passaging, recorded at the process step where cells are replated and cultured before differentiation; examples include mTeSR1 or Essential 8.

Passage number of the iPSC culture at the time of expansion/passaging, recorded as batch context immediately before the downstream differentiation step; typical values are low double digits for stable lines, such as 10 to 40.
Subculture split ratio used during passaging, recorded as the fraction or ratio applied when replating cells during maintenance expansion; examples include 1:4, 1:6, or 1:10.

Duration of the maintenance expansion interval associated with this passaging step, measured in hours from replating to the next maintenance change or transfer; typical range is 24 to 168 hours depending on growth rate.
Surface coating used for maintenance expansion during passaging, recorded as the substrate supporting adherent iPSC growth; examples include vitronectin, Matrigel, or laminin-521.
Approximate culture confluence at the time of passaging, recorded immediately before replating; typical range is 60 to 90 percent for routine iPSC maintenance.

Operator assessment of whether the iPSC culture met maintenance quality criteria at the passaging step, recorded before proceeding to differentiation; use to flag obvious morphology or contamination concerns.

expanded_ipscs.reasoning: This is an Entity node, so I included only intrinsic properties of the expanded iPSC culture state that result from maintenance expansion and are needed to hand off into differentiation. I focused on batch/context attributes that characterize the culture itself, not the passaging procedure details already captured on the upstream Process node and not the differentiation protocol or downstream neuronal outputs. I also avoided reusing donor identity and genetic provenance fields from the root Entity node, since those are already established upstream.

md_schema.descr: String identifier for the expanded iPSC culture batch at the time it is released for differentiation, recorded as the culture-level identity of the expanded state; example format: EXP_iPSC_001 or batch-aligned culture code.
Passage number associated with the expanded iPSC culture immediately before neuronal differentiation, recorded as the culture's current maintenance state; typical values are low to mid double digits.

Batch identifier linking the expanded iPSC culture to a specific maintenance/expansion batch, recorded as the stable culture batch context used for downstream differentiation and analysis; example format: BATCH_2024_01.
Estimated viable cell fraction in the expanded culture at release for differentiation, recorded at the handoff point from maintenance to differentiation; typical range is 70 to 100 percent.

Qualitative status of core pluripotency markers in the expanded culture at release, recorded as a culture-state quality attribute before differentiation; use this to indicate whether the expanded line retains pluripotent phenotype.
Contamination screening status for the expanded iPSC culture at the time of release for differentiation, recorded as a culture integrity check; use standardized lab screening results when available.

neuronal_differentiation_protocol.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included only the neuronal differentiation protocol parameters: how the expanded iPSCs were driven toward neuronal fate, including timing, factor regimen, media changes, and major culture conditions. I excluded upstream expanded-cell identity fields and downstream neuron properties because those belong on the Entity output node. I also did not include imaging, electrophysiology, or computational settings, since this step is a wet-lab differentiation process rather than capture or analysis. Existing fields from upstream Entity nodes already cover donor origin and batch identity, so I focused on protocol-specific implementation details needed to reproduce differentiation.

md_schema.descr: Name or short label of the neuronal differentiation protocol used to convert expanded iPSCs into neurons, recorded at the start of the process; example: dual-SMAD inhibition, NGN2 induction, or protocol-specific lab name.

Key growth factors, morphogens, or pathway inhibitors added during neuronal differentiation, recorded as the active factor set for this process step; examples include BDNF, GDNF, NT-3, SHH, CHIR99021, or SB431542.
Day in culture when neuronal differentiation was initiated from the expanded iPSC state, recorded as the process start point; typically day 0 relative to induction.

Total duration of the differentiation protocol from induction to the neuronal endpoint used for downstream analyses, measured in days; typical range depends on protocol and can span about 7 to 60 days.

Interval between differentiation medium refreshes during the protocol, measured in hours and recorded as the maintenance cadence for the differentiating cultures; examples include 24, 48, or 72 hours.

Mechanism used to induce neuronal fate in the expanded iPSCs, recorded as the central induction strategy for this process step; examples include small-molecule induction, transcription-factor transduction, or spontaneous differentiation.

Criterion used to decide when the differentiation process was complete and cultures were handed off to the differentiated-neuron entity state; examples include a fixed day, morphology threshold, or marker-expression milestone.

Seeding density of the expanded iPSC culture at the moment neuronal induction began, measured in cells per square centimeter; typical range is protocol dependent and must be recorded because it affects differentiation efficiency.

Operator or protocol-level assessment of whether the differentiation run met expected performance criteria, recorded at completion of the process; use to flag successful, partial, or failed induction runs.

differentiated_neurons.reasoning: This is an Entity node, so I included only intrinsic properties of the derived neuron culture as a finished biological material: culture identity, batch/protocol provenance carried forward from differentiation, maturation state, and basic neuronal identity markers. I excluded the differentiation procedure itself because that belongs to the upstream Process node, and I excluded morphology imaging, electrophysiology, and computed phenotype metrics because those belong to downstream Capture/Signal/Derivative nodes. I also avoided repeating donor-level iPSC provenance fields already established upstream, while keeping the neuron culture state distinct and usable as the handoff material for capture steps.

md_schema.descr: String identifier for the differentiated neuron culture or neuronal batch, recorded as the entity-level identity after differentiation; example format: NEUR_001 or batch-specific neuron culture code.

Batch identifier inherited from the neuronal differentiation run that produced this culture, recorded as the provenance link between the process and the differentiated neuron entity; example format: DIFF_BATCH_2024_03.

Concise summary of the differentiation timing associated with this neuron culture, recorded as the entity-level timing context after completion; examples include total differentiation days or key milestone days used by the originating protocol.

Maturation stage of the differentiated neurons at the time they are used for downstream capture, recorded as an intrinsic culture-state attribute; examples include progenitor-like, immature neuron, or mature neuron.

Qualitative status of expected neuronal marker expression in the differentiated culture, recorded at the entity level as a summary of neuronal identity; examples include MAP2-positive, TUJ1-positive, or synapsin-positive when those markers are assessed.

Overall health assessment of the differentiated neuron culture at the time of downstream use, recorded as the entity's usability state; use to flag whether the culture appears healthy, stressed, or compromised.

neuronal_morphology_capture.reasoning: This is a Capture node, so I included only microscope session and instrument-configuration fields that describe how the morphology measurement was acquired. I excluded sample properties of the differentiated neurons because those belong to the upstream Entity node, and I excluded raw image file properties because those belong to the downstream Signal node. I also did not include morphology feature definitions or computed phenotype summaries, since those are downstream Derivative territory. The fields focus on the configured imaging setup, acquisition mode, and operator-controlled settings needed to reproduce the capture session.

md_schema.descr: Manufacturer of the microscope used for neuronal morphology imaging, recorded as part of the instrument configuration for the capture session; example: Nikon, Zeiss, Leica, or Olympus.
Model name or number of the microscope used for morphology capture, recorded at the session level to identify the configured instrument; example: Ti2, LSM 880, or IX83.
Instrument serial number for the microscope used in this capture session, recorded to uniquely identify the hardware configuration; use the manufacturer-assigned serial string.
Microscopy modality used to record neuronal morphology, captured as the active imaging configuration for this session; examples include brightfield, phase contrast, fluorescence, or confocal.
Objective magnification used during morphology imaging, recorded at the time of capture; typical values are 10x, 20x, 40x, or 63x.
Effective pixel size of the acquired morphology images, measured in micrometers per pixel and recorded for the capture session; typical range depends on objective and camera settings.
Camera or detector exposure time used for each morphology image, measured in milliseconds at capture; record the operator-set value used for this session.
Relative illumination intensity used during morphology imaging, recorded as the percentage of maximum configured output at capture time; typically operator-set between 1 and 100 percent.
Whether a z-stack was acquired during the morphology capture session, recorded as a capture configuration flag; true if multiple focal planes were collected.
Names of the imaging channels actively collected in the morphology capture session, recorded as a session configuration summary; example values might include DAPI, MAP2, TUJ1, or phase channel.
Software used to control the microscope and acquire the morphology images, recorded as part of the capture setup; example: ZEN, NIS-Elements, or LAS X.
Version of the acquisition software used for the microscopy session, recorded to support reproduction of the capture settings; example format: 3.6 or 1.2.4.

raw_morphology_images.reasoning: This is a Signal node, so I included only raw data-artefact properties: file format, size, image dimensions, channel count, storage location, and technical quality metrics. I excluded microscope settings and acquisition software because those belong to the upstream Capture node, and I excluded any morphology interpretations or measurements because those belong to downstream Derivative nodes. I also avoided repeating biological sample provenance fields from the differentiated-neuron entity, since the Signal node should describe the file itself rather than the culture that produced it.

md_schema.descr: Digital file format of the raw morphology image data produced by the capture session, recorded as the stored artefact format; examples include TIFF, OME-TIFF, CZI, or ND2.
Size of the raw image file on disk, measured in bytes at the time of storage; use to estimate data volume and verify transfer completeness.
Width of the raw morphology image in pixels, recorded from the stored image artefact; typical values depend on camera and magnification.
Height of the raw morphology image in pixels, recorded from the stored image artefact; typical values depend on camera and magnification.
Number of imaging channels present in the raw morphology image file, recorded from the stored artefact; use this to describe multichannel acquisitions.
Number of z-planes contained in the raw image artefact, recorded when a z-stack was acquired; use 1 for single-plane images.
Storage location of the raw morphology image file, recorded as the file's access path or URI; example format: s3://bucket/path/file.tiff or local repository path.

Technical quality flag for the raw morphology image file, recorded after acquisition or ingestion to indicate whether the artefact is usable without major technical defects; examples include pass, warning, or fail.
Whether the raw image file contains embedded acquisition metadata in the file header or sidecar, recorded as a technical data-management property of the artefact.

Whether lossy or lossless compression was applied to the stored raw image artefact, recorded as a file-handling property that affects downstream reuse; examples include no compression, lossless compression, or lossy compression.

morphology_analysis.reasoning: This is a Process node for computational analysis, so I included only algorithm and processing parameters used to extract morphology features from the raw images, plus a limited output-quality indicator tied to the analysis run. I excluded raw image file properties because those belong to the upstream Signal node, and I excluded the resulting feature values and table dimensions because those belong to the downstream Derivative node. I also avoided capture/instrument fields and kept software details appropriate for a Process node because this step is executed by image-analysis software rather than by the microscope.

md_schema.descr: Name of the image-analysis software used to quantify neuronal morphology from the raw images, recorded as the computational agent for this process step; examples include CellProfiler, ImageJ/Fiji, or custom Python pipeline.
Version of the morphology analysis software or pipeline used for feature extraction, recorded to support reproducibility of the processing run; example format: 4.2.1 or 1.53c.

Repository URL or other source location for the morphology-analysis pipeline code, recorded when custom or version-controlled software is used; example format: https://github.com/org/repo or internal code archive link.

Method used to segment neurons or neurites before morphology measurement, recorded as the key image-processing strategy for this run; examples include threshold-based, machine-learning-based, or manual-assisted segmentation.

Approach used to compute morphology features after segmentation, recorded as the primary computational strategy for this analysis step; examples include skeletonization, contour analysis, or region-based measurement.

Minimum connected-object size retained during morphology analysis, measured in pixels and applied as a filtering threshold before feature extraction; typical values depend on magnification and segmentation approach.

Optional smoothing or regularization parameter applied during neuronal morphology analysis, recorded as the analysis-run setting that affects feature extraction; use the numeric value adopted by the pipeline.

Overall technical assessment of the morphology analysis run, recorded after processing to indicate whether the extracted features are reliable; use this to flag segmentation failures or incomplete runs.

morphology_features.reasoning: This is a Derivative node, so I included only computed-result fields describing the morphology feature table itself: what algorithmic output was produced, its dimensions, the kinds of features summarized, and a result-level quality indicator. I excluded raw image properties and analysis protocol parameters because those belong to the upstream Signal and Process nodes, respectively. I also avoided repeating specific feature values or biological sample provenance, since this node should describe the derived table as an analytical product rather than the input culture or capture setup.

md_schema.descr: Tabular or structured file format of the computed neuronal morphology features, recorded for the derived result artefact; examples include CSV, TSV, Parquet, or HDF5.

Count of individual neurons or segmented cell objects contributing to the morphology feature table, recorded as the derivation sample size for the computed result; typically ranges from tens to thousands depending on the assay.
Total number of morphology features computed and retained in the derived table, recorded as the dimensionality of the output; examples may include dozens to hundreds of features.

High-level categories of morphology descriptors included in the derived output, recorded as a summary of the computed result content; examples include soma size, neurite length, branching complexity, and polarity.
Method used to normalize morphology features in the derived table, recorded as a computation detail of the result; examples include z-score scaling, per-batch normalization, or no normalization.
Whether batch correction was applied to the computed morphology features before downstream analysis, recorded as a derivative-level processing indicator.

Overall quality assessment of the computed morphology feature table, recorded after derivation to indicate whether the output is suitable for downstream disease analysis; examples include pass, warning, or fail.
Storage location of the computed morphology feature table, recorded as the access path or URI for the derived artefact; example format: s3://bucket/path/features.csv or repository file path.
Runtime of the morphology feature derivation step, measured in minutes from analysis start to completion; recorded as an operational performance metric for the computed result pipeline.

synaptic_activity_capture.reasoning: This is a Capture node, so I included only the measurement-session and instrument-configuration fields for the electrophysiology acquisition used to record synaptic activity. I excluded neuron culture properties because those belong to the upstream Entity node, and I excluded trace-file and signal-format properties because those belong to the downstream Signal node. I also did not include derived activity metrics or interpretation, since those are downstream Process/Derivative territory. The fields emphasize hardware configuration, recording mode, and operator-controlled acquisition settings needed to reproduce the session.

md_schema.descr: Manufacturer of the electrophysiology rig used to capture synaptic activity from differentiated neurons, recorded as part of the instrument configuration for the session; example: Axon Instruments, HEKA, Multi Channel Systems, or Molecular Devices.
Model name or number of the electrophysiology system used for synaptic activity recording, recorded at the capture-session level; example: Axopatch 200B, PatchStar, or Maestro.
Serial number for the electrophysiology instrument used in this session, recorded to uniquely identify the hardware configuration; use the manufacturer-assigned serial string.
Electrophysiology recording mode used to capture synaptic activity, recorded as the active configuration for the session; examples include current clamp, voltage clamp, or extracellular recording.
Sampling rate used during synaptic activity capture, measured in hertz and recorded at acquisition time; typical values range from 1,000 to 50,000 Hz depending on mode and assay goals.

Low-pass or acquisition filter cutoff used during electrophysiology recording, measured in hertz and recorded as a session setting; typical values depend on recording mode and electrode configuration.

Holding potential applied during the synaptic activity recording session when relevant, measured in millivolts and recorded as a configured capture setting; use null-equivalent omission if not applicable.
Temperature of the recording environment during electrophysiology acquisition, measured in degrees Celsius at capture time; typical values are room temperature or near-physiological temperature.

Electrode or probe configuration used for synaptic activity recording, recorded as the session setup; examples include whole-cell patch pipette, multi-electrode array, or extracellular electrode array.
Software used to control the electrophysiology acquisition and record synaptic activity, recorded as part of the capture setup; example: pCLAMP, PatchMaster, LabChart, or AxoGraph acquisition.
Version of the acquisition software used for the synaptic activity capture session, recorded to support reproduction of the recording settings; example format: 11.2 or 3.6.1.

raw_activity_trace.reasoning: I revised the raw activity trace schema to remove fields that collided with already_generated metadata from other DAG steps. I retained only signal-specific properties that are still within the raw-data artefact territory and that do not duplicate upstream capture settings or downstream analysis outputs. The new fields focus on trace file structure and technical integrity while avoiding repeated file-size, sampling-rate, channel-count, storage-location, and generic quality-flag names.

md_schema.descr: Digital file format of the raw electrophysiology time-series, recorded as the stored artefact format; examples include ABF, EDF, CSV, or HDF5.
Duration of the recorded raw activity trace, measured in seconds as stored in the artefact; typically reflects the full capture episode.

Number of recording electrodes or acquisition inputs represented in the raw trace file, recorded from the stored artefact for multi-electrode or multi-channel recordings; typical values depend on the platform.
Whether obvious baseline drift is present in the raw activity trace, recorded as a technical signal-quality attribute of the artefact.
Whether the trace contains clipped or saturated segments, recorded as a technical quality defect flag for the raw signal artefact.
Whether event markers or annotations are embedded in the raw trace file, recorded as a file-content property of the signal artefact.

Alternative human-readable recording duration for the raw activity trace, measured in minutes when the stored artefact reports duration at a coarser granularity; use only if seconds are not available.
Units used for the raw trace time axis as stored in the artefact, recorded to clarify how time values are encoded; examples include seconds or milliseconds.
Units used for the primary signal amplitude in the raw trace, recorded from the artefact metadata when the file stores voltage- or current-based values; examples include millivolts or picoamperes.
Number of discrete recording segments, sweeps, or epochs contained in the raw activity trace file, recorded as a structural property of the stored artefact.

activity_analysis.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I kept only activity-analysis parameters that are specific to electrophysiology event derivation and avoided all fields previously generated elsewhere in the DAG, including generic software identity/version/repository fields and the generic analysis quality flag. I also excluded raw-trace properties and downstream metric outputs, since those belong to the Signal and Derivative nodes respectively. The remaining fields describe the computational method and key settings needed to reproduce synaptic activity metric extraction without colliding with prior metadata.

md_schema.descr: Amplitude threshold used to detect spikes or synaptic events in the raw electrophysiology trace, recorded as the primary event-detection setting for this process step; units should match the trace units, typically pA or mV.

Minimum number of detected events required to call a burst during activity analysis, recorded as the burst-detection rule applied to the trace; typical values are protocol-specific and often range from 2 to 10 events.

Window length used to smooth the raw trace or event rate before metric extraction, measured in seconds and recorded as an analysis parameter; typical values are fractions of a second to several seconds.
Duration of the baseline segment used for normalization or offset estimation in activity analysis, measured in seconds and recorded as the reference period for metric computation.

Method used to quantify evoked or spontaneous responses from the raw trace, recorded as the main metric-extraction strategy; examples include peak amplitude, area under curve, or frequency-based quantification.

Reference point used to align raw traces before activity metric calculation, recorded as the timing anchor for the analysis window; examples include stimulation onset, recording start, or event onset.

Core computational method used to derive synaptic activity metrics from the raw trace, recorded as the analysis strategy for this process step; examples include per-event summarization, sliding-window analysis, or frequency-domain analysis.

synaptic_activity_metrics.reasoning: This is still a Derivative node, so I kept only fields that uniquely describe the computed synaptic-activity output after avoiding all fields already generated elsewhere in the DAG, including number_of_cells_analyzed, normalization_method, result_quality_flag, and output_storage_uri. I focused on output content, dimensionality, thresholds/summary statistics, and a distinct result-quality concept that does not collide with prior generic quality fields. I excluded capture, raw trace, and analysis-process parameters because those belong upstream, and I avoided repeating prior derivative-level utility fields to satisfy the DAG-wide no-duplication rule.

md_schema.descr: Name of the synaptic activity metric set or feature catalog produced by the derivation, recorded as the identity of this computed output; example: firing-and-burst-summary or electrophysiology_feature_panel_v1.

Total number of individual synaptic activity metrics included in the derived result, recorded as the dimensionality of the output table or object; examples range from a handful of core metrics to dozens of event-derived features.

Number of detected synaptic events or spikes contributing to the derived activity metrics, recorded as the event support for the computed output; typical values depend on recording duration and cell responsiveness.
Scope of the computed synaptic activity summary, recorded to indicate whether the output describes spontaneous activity, evoked responses, or both.

Reference used for computing synaptic activity summaries in the derived output, recorded as the method for defining baseline or comparison state; examples include pre-stimulus baseline, rolling baseline, or no explicit reference.
Units used for response-amplitude metrics in the derived output, recorded for consistency of interpretation; examples include pA, mV, or arbitrary units depending on recording mode.

Threshold used in the derived output to define burst events or burst-like activity, recorded as a key summary parameter of the computed result; units depend on the event metric and should match the analysis definition.

Status flag describing whether the computed synaptic activity result was successfully produced and is internally consistent, recorded after derivation; use to distinguish successful output from partial or failed computation.
Runtime of the synaptic activity metric derivation step, measured in minutes from analysis start to completion; recorded as an operational performance metric for the computed result pipeline.

integrative_phenotype_analysis.reasoning: This is a Process node for computational integration, so I included only analysis-method and parameter fields that describe how morphology features and synaptic activity metrics were combined to evaluate disease phenotype and therapeutic response. I excluded upstream output-table properties because those belong to the morphology_features and synaptic_activity_metrics Derivative nodes, and I excluded the final combined report content because that belongs to the downstream Derivative node. I also avoided repeating any previously generated generic analysis fields, result-quality flags, output URIs, and common normalization/sample-count fields that were already used elsewhere in the DAG. The focus here is the integration strategy, weighting, and statistical/computational settings of the joint analysis.

md_schema.descr: Method used to combine morphology and synaptic activity outputs in the joint phenotype analysis, recorded as the core computational strategy for this process step; examples include feature concatenation, multi-view integration, canonical correlation, or machine-learning-based fusion.

Name of the bioinformatics software or analysis framework used for integrative phenotype analysis, recorded as the computational agent for this process step; examples include scikit-learn, R, Seurat-based workflow, or custom Python pipeline.
Version of the integration software or pipeline used to combine phenotype outputs, recorded to support reproducibility of the joint analysis; example format: 1.4.0 or 4.3.2.

Repository URL or source location for the integrative-analysis pipeline code, recorded when custom or version-controlled software is used; example format: https://github.com/org/repo or internal code archive link.

Relative weight assigned to morphology-derived features in the joint analysis, recorded as a numeric contribution parameter when weighted integration is used; typical range is 0 to 1 and should sum appropriately with other modality weights.

Relative weight assigned to synaptic activity metrics in the joint analysis, recorded as a numeric contribution parameter when weighted integration is used; typical range is 0 to 1 and should sum appropriately with other modality weights.

Method used to select or reduce features before the joint phenotype analysis, recorded as the preprocessing strategy for the combined dataset; examples include variance filtering, recursive feature elimination, or none.
Number of cross-validation folds used during integrative phenotype modeling, recorded when model evaluation is part of the joint analysis; typical values are 5 or 10.

Type of therapeutic response endpoint evaluated in the integrative analysis, recorded as the biological target of the combined phenotype model; examples include rescue of morphology, rescue of synaptic function, or composite phenotype improvement.

Overall technical assessment of the integrative phenotype analysis run, recorded after computation to indicate whether the joint analysis is suitable for downstream interpretation; use to flag failed model fitting or incomplete integration.

cellular_disease_phenotype_report.reasoning: This is a Derivative node, so I included only final report/result fields that describe the integrated phenotype output itself: report format, disease labels summarized, high-level phenotype findings, therapeutic-response interpretation, and a result-level quality flag. I excluded upstream modality-specific outputs and process parameters because those belong to morphology_features, synaptic_activity_metrics, and integrative_phenotype_analysis. I also avoided repeating common fields already generated elsewhere in the DAG such as output_storage_uri, generic analysis software, normalization, sample counts, and generic result-quality fields.

md_schema.descr: File or serialization format of the integrated cellular disease phenotype report, recorded as the final derived artefact format; examples include PDF, HTML, JSON, or CSV.

Disease category summarized by the integrated report, recorded as the cellular phenotype context for interpretation; examples include Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, or other neurodegenerative disease.

Concise textual summary of the combined cellular phenotype findings reported by the integrated analysis, describing morphology and synaptic-function patterns relevant to disease modeling and intervention assessment.

High-level summary of the inferred or observed response to a therapeutic intervention in the integrated report, recorded as the final disease-assessment outcome; examples include improved phenotype, partial rescue, no effect, or worsened phenotype.

Modalities that contributed to the final integrated report, recorded to document the evidence basis for the derived summary; use to indicate whether morphology, synaptic activity, or both were incorporated.

Numeric confidence or support score for the final integrated phenotype report, recorded as a summary-level assessment of how strongly the combined data support the stated interpretation; typical range is 0 to 1 when normalized.

Overall quality assessment of the final integrated report, recorded after derivation to indicate whether the summary is suitable for downstream review or reuse; use to flag incomplete or low-confidence reports.
Runtime of the final report-generation step, measured in minutes from analysis start to completion; recorded as an operational performance metric for the derived report.
